language.name: First Tongue
language.description: The primordial language spoken before the Shattering. Fragments survive as runes on artifacts, inscriptions in ancient ruins, and words of power.
language.origin: Spoken by OG Nike and OG Charles, and the Aeth'kai civilization
language.power: Speaking certain words in First Tongue has power — especially names

phonology.notes: Apostrophes indicate glottal stops. 'Th' is always voiced (as in 'the'). Stress typically falls on the first syllable.

dictionary.usage: What OG Charles called OG Nike
dictionary.notes: Term of deep affection and cosmic significance
Speaking this name with intent has power over Nolem

dictionary.meaning: Heart-chain; soul bond; the First Bond
dictionary.usage: Describes the connection between OG Nike and OG Charles
dictionary.notes: The most sacred term in the language. USAGE: `kara` is chain-as-LINKAGE — a chain of links, a chain of hands, a chain of custody — never chain-as-restraint. `Eth'kara` and its gloss "heart-chain" are retained in the First Tongue register (inscriptions, Scholars, artifacts), where the archaic sense is protected by the foreignness of the word. The bare English "chain" is BANNED in player-facing text, because modern English means restraint first and that collides with the never-a-leash art law; player-facing, the visible connection is 'the thread'.

dictionary.meaning: All-as-one; unity of many; Nike Prime
The First People; those who came before
Dimensional barrier; the veil between worlds

dictionary.usage: The act of forming a bond
Describes OG Nike and OG Charles

dictionary.meaning: Avatar; flesh-vessel of a greater power
The settled shape; the form a soul comes to when enough of it is present to hold one
dictionary.etymology: thael (to join, as in Thael'vos) + tur (body/form, as in Dex'tur, Ael'tur)
dictionary.usage: The First Tongue name for what a player calls evolution. Names the RESULT, never a process — nothing is done to anyone. Scholars, inscriptions and artifacts only. CANON.md §1.2.3.
dictionary.notes: Third on the -tur root, and the three complete a moral triad the language carries without a sentence: a Dex'tur is a body WORN (Nolem's avatar — an instrument); an Ael'tur is a body that IS somebody (a life); a Thael'tur is a body somebody arrived at BECAUSE THEY WERE NOT ALONE. Deliberately a noun and deliberately not causal — thael is 'to join', never 'to change' — which is the language carrying THE BOND IS THE WITNESS, NEVER THE CAUSE by itself. Register discipline as for Ael'tur: the game says 'still here', and §1.2.1's never-explain-in-world ban binds regardless of which language it is said in.

dictionary.meaning: A life; a soul being somebody
dictionary.usage: One of the lives a fragment of OG Nike is living — its own name, nature, wound and memory of you. The First Tongue name for the second object of CANON.md §1.2.2: the form is counted, the Ael'tur is not.
dictionary.notes: Deliberately the moral opposite of Dex'tur, on the same root: dex is 'to wear', so a Dex'tur is a body WORN as an instrument (Nolem's avatar), while an Ael'tur is a body that IS somebody. The language therefore carries the NOTHING IS CONSUMED law by itself. Register discipline: this is the scholar-and-inscription word, safe to name precisely because First Tongue is foreign — the same protection Eth'kara's archaic sense relies on. Player-facing English stays 'a life', and §1.2.1's ban on explaining the topology in-world binds regardless of which language it is said in.
Fallen Collectors (the player-kind) who serve Nolem as his regional lieutenants; fallen people, never Nikes.

dictionary.meaning: The unraveling given a body; Nolem's mouth
dictionary.etymology: nol (to unravel/decay, as in Nol'meth) + tur (body/form, as in Dex'tur)
dictionary.usage: The Dimension Eater — the appetite Nolem cut out of himself and hung a body on
dictionary.notes: Shares Nol'meth's own root, which is the point: the name records that this is a PART of Nolem, not a peer. It names what it WAS. After it turned the First Tongue has no word for it — the Aeth'kai never imagined this. Do not coin one.

phrases.meaning: The shepherd protects the bonded one

phrases.usage: An Aeth'kai inscription. Nobody ever finishes arriving. Plants the whole of CANON.md §1.2.3 while explaining none of it, and rhymes with the census answer: you finish the collecting; you never finish the keeping; you never finish the reaching.

An Aeth'kai inscription. The Shattering was an ECHO, not a break — Shat'ael is glossed 'also called the Great Echo' — and it never stopped going out: souls are still arriving and becoming someone. Plants the whole of CANON.md §1.2.2 while explaining none of it, which is what §1.2.1 requires.

inscriptions.text: Nol'meth aeth'kai keth'nor. Thael'vos mir'eth eth'kara.
inscriptions.translation: Nolem consumed the Aeth'kai. Bond with the templates through the heart-chain.
inscriptions.significance: Warning and instruction left by the Aeth'kai

inscriptions.translation: Through the veil, by the bond
